definitions.explanation: A romantic meeting or rendezvous, especially one that is secret or clandestine. Carries a literary, poetic nuance.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{逢瀬|おうせ}を{重|かさ}ねた。
examples.english: The two met in secret again and again.

examples.japanese: {人目|ひとめ}を{忍|しの}んで{逢瀬|おうせ}を{楽|たの}しんでいた。
examples.english: They enjoyed their secret meetings away from prying eyes.

examples.japanese: {小説|しょうせつ}の{主人公|しゅじんこう}たちは{月明|つきあ}かりの{下|もと}で{逢瀬|おうせ}を{果|は}たし、{互|たが}いの{想|おも}いを{確|たし}かめ{合|あ}った。
examples.english: The protagonists of the novel had their rendezvous by moonlight and confirmed their feelings for each other.

notes:
USAGE: {逢瀬|おうせ} is a literary and poetic word. It is rarely used in everyday conversation but appears frequently in novels, period dramas, and romantic literature. In casual speech, {密会|みっかい} (secret meeting) or simply デート would be used instead.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {逢瀬|おうせ}を{重|かさ}ねる (to meet in secret repeatedly)
- {逢瀬|おうせ}を{楽|たの}しむ (to enjoy a tryst)
- {逢瀬|おうせ}を{果|は}たす (to carry out a rendezvous)
- {人目|ひとめ}を{忍|しの}んで{逢瀬|おうせ}を... (to meet secretly away from prying eyes)

The kanji {逢|おう} means "to meet" (a more literary variant of {会|あ}う) and {瀬|せ} means "shallows" or "opportunity," giving the compound a sense of a fleeting, precious encounter.
